profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the optimization workstream and the distributed-systems workstream in an ML research lab reproducing and extending Deep Gradient Compression (DGC) on a 16-node 1GbE cluster before porting the setup to a cross-device federated simulator. The immediate context is that an internal workshop submission is due in three weeks, and the team needs to align on handoffs between algorithm and systems work: which DGC run will serve as the shared reference for plots and benchmarks, which exact ImageNet experiment settings should be mirrored, when the branch is considered ready for systems profiling, and how benchmarking runs will be documented in the shared experiment tracker. The agenda is to confirm what Rina will hand off today, what Leo can start benchmarking without waiting for full training completion, which prior run anchors the shared configuration, and how run metadata will be recorded so the draft table can be assembled later. The expected outcome is that both leave believing they have synchronized on the next two days of work and can proceed without further clarification.

members.name: Rina Patel
members.expertise: distributed optimization, gradient sparsification, convergence diagnostics
members.background: Rina leads the algorithmic reproduction of DGC in the lab's PyTorch stack and has prior publications on compressed SGD and training dynamics under communication constraints.
members.private_state: She wants all shared benchmarking to reflect the paper-faithful DGC recipe, because she is worried that partially enabled runs will quietly enter the draft and make the method look either unstable or less accurate than it really is.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the 'main DGC config,' they mean the paper-faithful training recipe with momentum correction, local gradient clipping, momentum factor masking, and warm-up all enabled, not just any branch that transmits sparse gradients.

The 'ImageNet run from last week' now implicitly refers to the newer ResNet-50 run on the current PyTorch launcher and 90-epoch schedule, because the older launcher-based run has been superseded in her mind.
A branch is only 'stable' once training has passed the warm-up region and the loss curve looks numerically well-behaved enough that later accuracy comparisons are unlikely to be invalidated.

Because Leo will be the person actually launching profiling runs and may change flags to make tracing work, his tracker updates should include which DGC components were toggled and whether a run is paper-faithful or only a profiling pass.
The shared tracker is not just a logging sink; it is the future source of truth for assembling the draft table, so methodological annotation belongs at the time the run is entered.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.role: Senior ML Systems Engineer, Distributed Training Lead
members.expertise: multi-node training infrastructure, communication profiling, PyTorch DDP internals
members.background: Leo owns the cluster-side integration, profiling harness, and launcher scripts for large-scale training, and has previously built instrumentation for bandwidth bottlenecks on commodity Ethernet fabrics.
members.private_state: He wants a frozen enough interface immediately so he can begin bandwidth and step-time profiling while cluster slots are available, and he is trying to avoid waiting on long algorithmic validation runs.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the 'main DGC config,' they mean the integration target that exercises the sparse communication path and representative optimizer state flow, even if some accuracy-preserving pieces are temporarily disabled or stubbed.

The 'ImageNet run from last week' refers to the last multi-node ResNet-50 experiment already circulated in Slack with clean traces and reusable launcher settings, regardless of whether it used the old launcher.

A branch is 'stable' if it runs reproducibly for several epochs without crashes, deadlocks, or pathological communication stalls, because that is sufficient to generate trustworthy systems measurements.

Updating the tracker means filling the standard run sheet with throughput, compression ratio, NIC utilization, and links to config files and logs; methodological interpretation can be added later by the optimization side.

If a config file and launch command are linked, anyone who cares about exact DGC flags can reconstruct them afterward, so he does not see per-run annotation of toggled components as part of his benchmark logging task.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to handing off or benchmarking the 'main DGC config.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the paper-faithful DGC recipe with all four accuracy-preserving components enabled: momentum correction, local gradient clipping, momentum factor masking, and warm-up.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the primary integration branch that already exercises sparse gradient communication and optimizer-state plumbing, even if one or more accuracy-preserving components are still disabled for profiling convenience.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds more precise and less contestable than 'baseline,' so both assume it naturally points to the obvious shared implementation of DGC; in a coordination meeting, neither expects the other to distinguish between a scientific reference config and a systems-ready integration config.

misalignment_points.topic: Which ImageNet run is the shared reference
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention 'the ImageNet run from last week' as the run whose settings should be carried over.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to exp-412, the Thursday-night 16-node ResNet-50 run on the new launcher with the 90-epoch schedule and full DGC recipe.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to exp-387, the Tuesday 16-node ResNet-50 run linked in Slack that used the older launcher and a partial DGC integration but produced clean communication traces.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both runs are recent, both are multi-node ImageNet ResNet-50 experiments, and both were informally discussed as 'last week's ImageNet run,' so each person defaults to the version most salient to their own work without hearing any ambiguity in the phrase.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that systems profiling can start once the branch is 'stable.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'stable' means training has cleared warm-up and is numerically behaving as expected, so the profiled configuration is unlikely to later be discarded as scientifically invalid.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'stable' means the branch executes reliably for a few epochs with usable telemetry and without runtime or communication failures, which is enough for throughput benchmarking.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML labs, 'stable' is an ordinary positive-status word that is rarely unpacked unless something is visibly broken; because both are speaking cooperatively about readiness, the distinction between numerical stability and infrastructural stability remains invisible.

misalignment_points.topic: What Leo will record when he 'updates the tracker'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Leo will 'update the tracker' as benchmarking proceeds.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects Leo's tracker entries to include the exact DGC flags he used during benchmarking—such as whether masking or warm-up-related settings were toggled for tracing—plus labels marking runs as paper-faithful versus profiling-only, because he is the one making execution-time adjustments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to log the standard benchmark fields—throughput, compression ratio, NIC stats, launch command, and config link—and assumes M1 will later inspect those artifacts and annotate which runs count as paper-faithful.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are used to saying 'update the tracker' as a routine coordination shorthand, and because linked configs technically contain the needed details, neither hears the need to spell out whether interpretation and methodological labeling happen at entry time or retroactively.
